name: Employer compliance kit for third-country workers (permits, police-district limit, A1.1 language test, board-member work permits)
buyer: Small employers and labour agencies in construction, hospitality, transport and delivery that hire foreign workers
trigger: Zakon o izmjenama i dopunama Zakona o strancima (NN 55/26, in force 4 June 2026): employer must run an active registered business tied to the job; worker limited to the police district where the labour-market test was done; A1.1 Croatian exam after one year for HZZ-opinion permits; work permit for board members who are third-country nationals within 30 days of court-register entry; change of employer after 6 months; fines 5,000-20,000 EUR (legal persons) from the 2025 law.
evidence: rrif.hr/izmjene_zakona_o_strancima_stupaju_na_snagu_4_lipn-2521-vijest/; crowe.com/hr/news/sto-nam-donose-nove-izmjene-zakona-o-strancima; index.hr article on stricter employer rules; HGK seminar on 7 Oct 2026 about foreign workers and new employer duties.
existing: No dedicated competitor search run (budget overrun by one search). Generic HR and payroll tools likely cover part of it; a permit-expiry and document tracker for small employers was not found in the results.
unchecked: Final seasonal-permit rules; whether employers must keep a register; number of small employers affected; competitor search ('program evidencija stranih radnika dozvole'); risk that it is generic HR software.

first_check.duty: Zakon o strancima as amended by NN 55/26 (in force 4.6.2026). Only an employer that actively carries out the registered business tied to the job can get a permit. A worker hired after a labour-market test may work only in that police district. Change of employer is allowed after 6 months. Under Art. 95, the employer must notify police within 15 days when the contract or another permit condition ends. Fine for a legal person under Art. 251: 660-920 EUR, plus 60-390 EUR for the responsible person, as cited in Varaždin court decisions. Courts have often prosecuted this. Seasonal permits must be renewed at least 15 days before expiry. Under the workers' records rulebook (Pravilnik o evidencijama o radnicima), the permit or work registration certificate is a mandatory field. Corrections to the claim: the A1.1 exam obligation is postponed to 4.6.2027. The 30-day board-member rule and the 5,000-20,000 EUR fines were not verified.
first_check.market: MUP 2024: 172,499 residence and work permits (68,912 construction, 45,868 tourism and hospitality). About 117,549 foreign workers held valid permits at the end of 2024. MUP: 213k applications by October 2025. HUP expects more than 200k foreign workers. The number of employers is not published; it is likely in the low tens of thousands (estimate, not verified).
first_check.competitor: No Croatian tool for tracking permits or expiry dates was found in three searches. Foreign products exist (HRappka in Poland, SAP SuccessFactors Visa & Permits, Pandahrms). The state HZZ/MUP application covers filing, but news reports say it is buggy and has no status tracking. Employment agencies, lawyers and accountants do the core permit work as a service. Croatian payroll and HR vendors (e.g. modules for workers' records) were not checked one by one, so there is a risk this is a generic HR-document feature.
first_check.reason: The duty is real. NN 55/26 has been in force since 4 June 2026 and adds the active-business test, a limit to the police district where the labour-market test was done, and easier change of employer. Two details in the claim are wrong. The Croatian language exam is postponed to 4 June 2027. The 5,000-20,000 EUR fines were not verified; the fine I found for late notice to police is 660-920 EUR. Courts do prosecute these cases often. I found no Croatian product that tracks permits, but the core job (applying for permits) is done by the HZZ/MUP portal plus agencies and lawyers. That leaves a tracker for expiry dates and 15-day notices, which is close to generic HR software. Volume is high: 172,499 permits in 2024.

challenge_check.killer: None found. The partial substitutes are service providers (Manpower Croatia, EOR platforms like Deel and Gloroots), generic expiry-tracking HR modules (Odoo hr-employee-documents-expiry), and the state filing tools (HZZ platform, MUP Burza rada app), which do not track ongoing compliance.
challenge_check.reason: I ran seven searches, in Croatian and English, and found nothing that kills this. No Croatian product tracks foreign workers' permits, expiry dates or 2026-law duties. The state tools only handle filing: the HZZ online platform covers 90-day seasonal permits, and other requests go to the police by e-mail. Status tracking was only planned. The market is real: MUP issued 94,113 permits in H1 2026 (36,601 renewals), mostly in tourism and construction. I could not find how many employers that is. Score stays modest because three things already cover the job: agencies, lawyers and EOR firms (Manpower, Deel) do permit work as a service; generic document-expiry modules exist (Odoo add-on); and the workflow is mostly reminders plus checklists.
